items.title: Hurricanes Place Taylor Hall On IR
items.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes have placed winger Taylor Hall on injured reserve, opening up a roster spot.
items.body: Register Login Hurricanes Place Taylor Hall On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 19, 2026 7:30 pm The Hurricanes made a move to open up a roster spot on Monday, announcing that they’ve placed winger Taylor Hall on injured reserve. No immediate corresponding recall was made, leaving Carolina’s active roster at 22 players for the time being; they’re next in action on Tuesday. The 34-year-old sustained an upper-body injury last Tuesday against Washington. While there’s no firm timeline for his return, head coach Rod Brind’Amour recently noted that Hall is expected to be out week-to-week. Accordingly, it was only a matter of time before he landed on IR. Hall’s injury derailed what had been a strong start to his season. After finding another gear offensively in the playoffs when he had 19 points in as many games, he picked up three goals and two assists in eight games in the early going to this campaign. That had him on an early pace to surpass the 50-point mark for only the second time this decade but that will be considerably more challenging now given that he’ll miss at least a few weeks of action. Carolina’s recent injuries have allowed them to give looks to youngsters Bradly Nadeau and Felix Under Sorum. In the short term, it’s likely that they’ll continue to get some chances but with Hall’s placement, they now have the ability to recall someone else from AHL Chicago in the near future. With Mark Jankowski being evaluated for an injury sustained on Saturday against Winnipeg, that recall could be coming soon as they’re down to just 12 healthy forwards on their active roster.

items.title: Report: Trial set for man accused of killing Gaudreau brothers
items.summary: The man accused of killing NHL star Johnny Gaudreau and his brother Matthew will stand trial early next year.
items.body: The man accused of killing NHL star Johnny Gaudreau and his brother Matthew will stand trial early next year. Sean Higgins is facing two counts of first-degree aggravated manslaughter, two counts of second-degree reckless vehicular homicide, and one count each of tampering with physical evidence and leaving the scene of a fatal accident. Jury selection in Salem County, N.J., will begin on Dec. 1 and the trial will begin on Jan. 4 after a holiday break, according to The Athletic and ABC Action News 6 in Philadelphia. Higgins, 45, appeared in court on Monday and rejected a plea agreement. He faces up to 91 1/2 years in prison if found guilty of all charges, Superior Court Judge Michael Silvanio said in court on Monday, according to The Athletic . Johnny Gaudreau, who played 11 seasons in the NHL with the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets , and his brother Matthew Gaudreau died on Aug. 29, 2024, after they were struck by a car while riding their bikes near their family's home in rural New Jersey. Johnny was 31 and Matthew was 29.

items.title: Cole Knuble, son of Mike Knuble, makes NHL debut with Flyers
items.summary: On Monday night, he made his NHL debut for the team he grew up rooting for, with his parents in attendance.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Cole Knuble has fond memories of the Philadelphia Flyers ' home arena from his father, Mike, playing for them during his lengthy career. On Monday night, he made his NHL debut for the team he grew up rooting for, with his parents in attendance. The 22-year-old was one of three players called up from Lehigh Valley of the American Hockey League to fill in for injured forwards Owen Tippett, Tyson Foerster and Travis Konecny against Colorado. “Obviously I have been a fan of this team my whole life, so I think it’s extra special,” Knuble said. A fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft, Knuble nearly made the team out of training camp. He was disappointed to get sent to the minors but quickly adjusted his thinking. “I came (to camp) trying to make the team,” Knuble said. “But I think once I got down to Lehigh, the staff was so great. The players were all very welcoming, and I got to play in every situation. If you’re doing that, you can’t really complain too much, and I get an opportunity every game to kind of showcase myself and it’s a lot of fun.” Mike Knuble played 362 games, counting playoffs, with Philadelphia from 2005-09 and 2013.

items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Cole Schwindt; Reassign Sam Lafferty By Brennan McClain | at October 19, 2026 6:00 pm According to a team announcement , the Florida Panthers recalled forward Cole Schwindt from the AHL’s Charlotte Checkers. In a corresponding roster move, the Panthers assigned forward Sam Lafferty the other way. Schwindt, 25, recently played his first AHL contests since the 2023-24 season, then with the Calgary Flames. Since the Panthers entered the 2026-27 campaign relatively healthy, Schwindt didn’t make Florida’s opening-night roster. He has performed relatively well with the Checkers, scoring one goal and three points in five games with a -1 rating. Still, Schwindt earned an extended stay with the Panthers last season because the team dealt with so many injuries. He was on that list early in the season, fracturing his arm in November, which caused him to miss several months. He finished the campaign with five goals and seven points in 29 games with a +2 rating, averaging 10:02 of ice time per game. Meanwhile, Lafferty is headed to AHL Charlotte to delay his waiver eligibility. The eight-year NHL veteran was recalled on October 3rd after captain Aleksander Barkov was injured. On the roster since then, Lafferty was only five games and/or 14 days from requiring waivers for reassignment again. Furthermore, Lafferty didn’t start great. Joining the Panthers this past offseason on a one-year, $850K contract, Lafferty went scoreless in five games with a -4 rating. Even though he began over 70% of his shifts in the offensive zone, Lafferty won only eight of his 32 draws. He also owns the worst CorsiFor on the team at 36.4% in all situations.

items.body: Register Login Islanders Issue Injury Updates By Brennan McClain | at October 19, 2026 5:00 pm Despite defeating the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday, the New York Islanders lost a pair of top-six forwards to lower-body injuries . Both Calum Ritchie and Matias Maccelli exited the game in the first period, and the Islanders issued firm recovery timelines for each of them today. According to New York’s announcement, Ritchie will miss the next four to six weeks, and Maccelli will miss the next two to four weeks. Earlier this morning, concern for Ritchie and Maccelli’s availability peaked after the Islanders recalled Mitchell Chaffee on an emergency basis and moved defenseman Alexander Romanov to the injured reserve. It’s a difficult blow for the Islanders to absorb, especially because they’ve been without center Mathew Barzal through their first eight contests of the 2026-27 season. Barzal is expected back relatively soon, but New York’s forward corps could be shorthanded for another month after he returns. Offensively, the Islanders don’t have much room for error. items.summary: The Vancouver Canucks provided an update on their injured goaltender.
items.body: The Vancouver Canucks provided an update on their injured goaltender. Speaking to reporters Monday, head coach Manny Malhotra addressed the latest status of Thatcher Demko . Most notably, the first-year NHL coach said, "To my knowledge, no," when asked if there was any concern Demko might not play in the 2026-27 season. "It's a slow process for him, but he is getting better," said Malhotra about Demko's recovery from hip surgery in January 2026. "Again, don't want to put a timeline on him, but the fact he is improving daily is a positive. But we've said from Day 1 we're not in a situation where we're in a rush." Demko was spotted at the Canucks' practice on Monday, watching from the bench . When asked if the veteran netminder is currently on the ice at all, Malhotra answered, "In this last week, I think we dialled it back. So I think he took a couple days off the ice this (past) weekend." Demko, who signed a three-year, $25.5-million extension with the Canucks in July 2025, went 8-10-1 with an .897 save percentage, a 2.90 goals-against average and one shutout last season over 20 games. He missed a stretch of games from mid-November to mid-December with a lower-body injury, then returned and appeared in 10 more contests before going down again. items.body: The Buffalo Sabres may have their captain back sooner rather than later. Rasmus Dahlin told reporters on Monday that he's "ready" to return after missing the team's last three games with an upper-body injury. The Sabres defenceman took part in practice on Monday for the first time since Oct. 11 and is expected to suit up against the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday. “I think I’ll be ready. We’ll see here tomorrow and go from there,” Dahlin said. His injury occurred last week in a win against the Florida Panthers, when he left early in the second period while reaching for his back after putting a shot on goal. Dahlin exited after 7:08 of ice time in the first period, chipping in a goal as part of the 5-3 victory. Speaking to reporters on Monday, the Norris Trophy finalist from a year ago made it clear he wasn't all too concerned with the injury. “I knew it wasn’t going to be long, let’s just say that. I didn’t think it was going to take a full week.” “He had a couple good days while we were gone,” Sabres coach Lindy Ruff added. “Got him back in practice and see how he handles that today. But I thought he looked good.” Dahlin has two goals and two assists through six games this season. Once back on the ice, the 26-year-old will try to replicate his stellar production from a year ago, when he racked up a career-high 74 points (19 goals, 55 assists) in 77 regular-season appearances. He then added another four goals and 10 helpers in 13 games during the Sabres playoff run — the franchise's first post-season berth since 2011.

items.summary: Some NHL teams are using their emergency backup goalies in practice and bringing them on the road.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The NHL is requiring each team to have a full-time emergency backup goalie on its roster, under the new collective bargaining agreement. Some teams are going one step further. NHL.com correspondent Kevin Woodley wrote a piece last week on how EBUGs can help full-time netminders with load management throughout the season. Several NHL teams have their EBUGs travel with them on the road, and others used theirs to take the majority of shots in practice. On a special Monday roundtable episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Woodley joins former NHL goaltenders Carter Hutton and Devan Dubnyk to discuss EBUGs and how the role has evolved in the last few years. You might take five good reps then you have to back off. At some point, it’s diminishing returns and you’re not doing yourself any good. You’re just out there as target practice. On Monday, the Philadelphia Flyers placed forward Owen Tippett on injured reserve. In response, the team called up forward Jacob Gaucher from its American Hockey League affiliate, the Lehigh Valley Phantoms. Tippett was last seen in the lineup last Thursday, when the Flyers visited the Detroit Red Wings . It isn’t clear whether the 27-year-old was hurt during the team’s 2-1 loss, as he played the entire game, logging 15:36 of ice time and posting a -1 plus/minus. However, in Philadelphia’s Saturday matchup with the Ottawa Senators , Tippett was ruled out with an upper-body injury. The Flyers pulled out a 3-1 win, the team’s first victory of the season. Per the NHL’s IR rules, he’ll be ineligible to return to the lineup until this coming Saturday, when the Flyers host the Anaheim Ducks. Coming off a solid 51-point performance during the 2025-26 season, Tippett, along with the rest of the team around him, has struggled to find his groove early on this year. In nine appearances thus far, the Peterborough, Ont. native has scored just one goal and one assist. He has a -2 rating while averaging 16:26 of ice time per game. items.summary: Duehr has yet to play this season due to a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Terrence Lee-Imagn Images A veteran forward is now up for grabs in the NHL. On Monday, the Winnipeg Jets placed winger Walker Duehr on waivers, making him eligible to be claimed by any of the other 31 NHL teams. If Duehr clears waivers, the Jets can assign him to their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Manitoba Moose. The Sioux Falls, South Dakota native has yet to play this season due to a lower-body injury he sustained during Winnipeg’s preseason. He was medically cleared and able to fully join Jets practice on Friday, and is now being waived with the intent of sending him to the AHL. Duehr, 28, went scoreless in three games for Winnipeg last season. In 62 games for Manitoba, he notched 17 goals and 17 assists for 34 points, before contributing a goal and two assists for three points in the team’s seven playoff games. After a four-year collegiate career with Minnesota State University, Mankato, Duehr signed with the Calgary Flames as an undrafted free agent in April of 2021. In three-plus seasons with the Flames’ organization, he played a total of 84 NHL games while totaling nine goals and 10 assists for 19 points. In January of 2025, Duehr was waived by Calgary and claimed by the San Jose Sharks . In eight games for San Jose over the remainder of the 2024-25 season, he had two goals and no assists. Ahead of the 2025-26 season, Duehr signed a one-year, two-way contract with the Jets. This past offseason, he signed a two-year, $1.75 million deal to stay with Winnipeg. The Jets, who have gotten off to a solid start with a 4-2-2 record for 10 points through eight games this season, will begin a miniature two-game road trip against the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday before visiting the Dallas Stars on Thursday.

items.title: How hard is it to mentally prepare after going from NHL backup to starter?
items.summary: Goaltending in the NHL is a tough gig, so the toll on a starter is different than on a backup.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Goaltending in the NHL is a tough gig. You’ve got to stop a piece of vulcanized rubber coming at you speeds of 60 to 90 miles per hour about 30 times per game, and if you don’t do so often enough, you’ll get the lion’s share of blame for your team’s struggles. It’s no wonder, then, that the mental toll for a starter is much different than that of a backup. Take Vancouver Canucks goaltender Leevi Merilainen, for example. In a backup role with the Ottawa Senators during the 2024-25 season, he shone with .925 save percentage and a 1.99 goals-against average in 12 appearances. Briefly thrust into the starter’s spot last season in the absence of Senators starter Linus Ullmark, he struggled with a .860 SV% and a 3.51 GAA in 20 appearances. In a more part-time role with Vancouver this season, Merilainen is looking more like his self from two years ago. Their voyage from Southern California to New York took 15 hours with a three-hour time difference tossed into the mix. The travel day started at 8:30 a.m. PT. items.title: Senators’ Thomas Chabot out one to two weeks with upper-body injury
items.body: The Ottawa Senators will be without their captain for the foreseeable future. Newly extended head coach Travis Green told reporters on Monday that the forward was "going to be out, probably ... a week to two weeks," with an upper-body injury. Chabot left Saturday's 3-1 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers with the injury and was seen shaking his hand in the penalty box during the first period before exiting. He was a minus-1 with one shot on goal in 12:03 of ice time through the first two periods. While it's unclear when exactly the injury occurred, Green did reveal that Chabot had been playing banged-up before Saturday. "He played a game with (the injury) ... it might have been the game before the last one," Green said. "It happened early, finished the game, and then he thought he would be fine, but couldn't go." Chabot was named the 11th captain in Senators history ahead of the season (and became the first francophone to wear the "C" in Ottawa), replacing Brady Tkachuk, who was traded to the Florida Panthers. The 30-year-old had posted one goal and three assists for a plus-5 through nine games before injury.

The 29-year-old finished his week with an electric five-point performance in the Oilers' 6-2 win over the Utah Mammoth on Saturday. items.summary: Swayman has the Bruins on a hot start in the opening weeks of the 2026-27 season, and is looking like one of the best in the NHL.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images One of the hottest teams in the NHL in the early weeks of the 2026-27 season is the Boston Bruins, with a lot of thanks going to their netminder. After a bumpy 2024-25 season following an elongated contract dispute, Bruins goaltender Jeremy Swayman has shown why he earned an eight-year contract, especially this year. The 27-year-old has helped Boston reestablish itself as one of the top teams in the Atlantic Division, with the team currently fighting for the top spot in the Eastern Conference. While there’s a lot of hockey to be played in the expanded 84-game regular season, Swayman has been a key part of the B’s exceptional start to the young campaign. In seven games, Swayman has a record of 6-1-0, tied with former teammate and Ottawa Senators star Linus Ullmark, as well as the Minnesota Wild’s Jesper Wallstedt, for the most wins so far in the NHL. Swayman also has a 1.85 goals-against average, a .934 save percentage and one shutout. If he can find some consistency and keep those numbers the same for most of the season, we might see Swayman in the Vezina Trophy conversation. Even in a league with so many talented netminders, Swayman has the ability to be a gamechanger for the Bruins, something that can put him in line for an award. On Monday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , former NHL netminder Devan Dubnyk explains why Swayman deserves to be in the Vezina Trophy. Devan Dubnyk: I think that Boston is looking pretty damn good, and he’s kind of been, I mean, he’s always been great. He’s obviously had his one down year, but I think this year he just looks as good as he has. When he’s going, he’s lights out. I think Boston’s got a good squad too.

items.title: Canadiens notebook: Lefty-righty defence balance boosted by Reinbacher
items.summary: David Reinbacher has given the Montreal Canadiens the ability to play three lefty-righty defensive pairs. Eric Engels explains how having that consistency on the blue line opens up so much for the Habs.
items.body: BROSSARD, Que.— Saturday’s game against the Buffalo Sabres presented an opportunity to not only see David Reinbacher in action, but also to see what the Montreal Canadiens look like with three perfectly balanced defence pairings all featuring legitimate NHL talent. We hadn’t seen enough of either since Martin St. Louis stepped behind the bench in February of 2022. Not of Reinbacher, who’s been plagued by injuries since being taken fifth overall by the Canadiens in June of 2023, and certainly not of three lefty-righty combos giving St. Louis all the optionality he looks for in different situations. items.title: Connor McDavid enters rarified air with early-season points pace
items.summary: At this point, we must carve out a minute simply to appreciate the magic of Oilers superstar Connor McDavid. Ryan Dixon explains why.
items.body: At this point, we must carve out a minute simply to appreciate Connor McDavid ’s magic. McDavid recorded his second five-point game of the fledgling season on Saturday during Edmonton’s 6-2 smashing of a good Mammoth club in Utah. McDavid is up to 23 points through eight contests, and the only player in the history of the league to better that pace is Mario Lemieux. If you can believe it, No. 66 put up 27 points in eight games in both 1995-96 and 1992-93, while — wait for it — producing 31 points in eight games to begin the 1988-89 campaign. During that latter season, Lemieux nearly became the second player in NHL history to record a 200-point season when he finished with 199 in 76 games. Just over 35 years later, we can officially sit here and wonder if McDavid can join Wayne Gretzky as the second member of the 200-point club. (Gretzky did it four times, all in five seasons from 1981-82 through 1985-86.) McDavid has a little extra grace as the NHL features an 84-game schedule this season, four more than the 80-game slate Gretzky was playing in the early 1980s. Sure, the double-century club feels unattainable, but McDavid could be held off the scoresheet in his next game and still be on pace for 215 points. And if he happens to pick up a couple points in each of his next two outings, he’ll be tracking better than a 225-point showing. items.summary: Green has led the Senators to two consecutive playoff appearances, their first since 2017.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mar 5, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Ottawa Senators head coach Travis Green on his bench during the first period against the Calgary Flames at Scotiabank Saddledome. Mandatory Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images The Ottawa Senators announced Monday that they have signed head coach Travis Green to a multi-year contract extension. Green, 55, is in his third season behind the Ottawa bench. Through Monday, he’s posted a record of 95-60-18 with a points percentage of .601. He’s led the Senators to two consecutive Stanley Cup Playoff appearances — their first since 2017. “When I was in the search to identify our head coach two years ago, it was clear to me that Travis had the qualities to move our team forward,” general manager Steve Staios said in a news release. “I have watched him implement systems and structures that have reinforced my belief in his coaching abilities. We share the same vision and philosophy and are confident we can continue to build on our team.” Green, a native of Castlegar, B.C., has nine seasons of experience as an NHL head coach. He spent four-and-a-half years behind the bench with the Vancouver Canucks between 2017-18 and 2021-22, leading them through the playoffs in 2020. He also had a short stint with the New Jersey Devils in 2023-24. As a player, Green played 14 seasons in the NHL, where he scored 193 goals and added 262 assists for 455 points and 764 penalty minutes in 970 regular-season games with the New York Islanders , Anaheim Ducks , Arizona Coyotes, Toronto Maple Leafs and Boston Bruins . He was part of the Leafs’ 2002 Eastern Conference Final run, where he recorded three goals and six assists for nine points in 20 games.

items.title: Rangers sign Luke Glendening to PTO
items.summary: Glendening failed to make the Tampa Bay Lightning roster out of training camp.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images A veteran center is getting another shot to play in the NHL. On Monday, the New York Rangers announced that the team has signed forward Luke Glendening to a professional tryout agreement. Under the agreement, which is limited to just 10 days, Glendening can’t play in any regular-season games for the Blueshirts, but can practice and train with the team. This is the second time in just over a month that Glendening is attempting to crack a roster. He attended the Tampa Bay Lightning ‘s training camp earlier this fall on a PTO , but failed to earn a new contract. That’s certainly unlike what happened during the 2025-26 season. The 37-year-old signed a PTO with the New Jersey Devils ahead of the preseason before signing a one-year, $775,000 contract. The East Grand Rapids, Mich. native wasn’t with the Devils for the entire season. Just before the trade deadline, the veteran center was placed on waivers and was claimed by the Philadelphia Flyers . Glendening found a little bit of production with his new team, scoring two goals and five points in 18 regular-season games as the Flyers finished third in the Metropolitan Division, clinching a spot in the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the first time in six years. The University of Michigan product scored one goal in 10 postseason contests as Philadelphia reached the second round before falling to the eventual Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . In 70 overall games last year, Glendening scored two goals and seven assists for nine points. In 934 regular-season NHL games, including stints with the Detroit Red Wings and Dallas Stars , Glendening has posted 85 goals and 90 assists for 175 points, plus 11 points in 60 playoff contests.

He scored his second goal and played a season-high 17:08 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Oct. 13 that gave him five points (two goals, three assists) during a four-game point streak. Hiller said at a certain point he realized McKenna had sat so long, "I said, I'm not going put him out there now. I've been sitting him there for 30 minutes. It's not fair to him." The two spoke Friday and McKenna said Hiller told him, "It had nothing to do with my play, which is obviously nice to know." items.body: Forward injured in victory against Capitals on Tuesday; Jarvis close to making season debut Taylor Hall is week to week for the Carolina Hurricanes because of an upper-body injury. The 34-year-old forward left during the second period of a 4-2 win against the Washington Capitals on Tuesday. "We've got kind of a week-to-week situation happening," Hurricanes coach Rod Brind'Amour said Friday. "So ask me again in a week." Hall has five points (three goals, two assists) in eight games this season. He had 19 points (seven goals, 12 assists) in 19 Stanley Cup Playoff games to help Carolina win the Cup last season. He is three games shy of 1,000 in the NHL, with 792 points (305 goals, 487 assists) in 997 games for the Edmonton Oilers, New Jersey Devils, Arizona Coyotes, Buffalo Sabres, Boston Bruins, Chicago Blackhawks and Hurricanes. Selected by the Oilers with the No. 1 pick in the 2010 NHL Draft, he won the Hart Trophy, voted as the League's most valuable player, with the Devils in 2017-18, when he had an NHL career-high 93 points (39 goals, 54 assists) in 76 games. Carolina (7-2-1), already without captain Jordan Staal for 1-2 months because of a calf tear, won seven straight before Sunday's 3-2 loss to the Calgary Flames. They're also waiting for forward Seth Jarvis to make his season debut after having shoulder surgery in June to repair a torn labrum and rotator cuff in his right shoulder. items.title: Sharangovich nets winner as Flames snap Hurricanes’ seven-game win streak
items.body: Morgan Frost scored once and set up Yegor Sharangovich's late game-winner as the Calgary Flames beat Carolina 3-2 on Sunday night, snapping the Hurricanes' seven-game winning streak. Matvei Gridin also scored for Calgary (2-6-0), which won for the first time in four games on home ice. Jesperi Kotkaniemi and Jalen Chatfield scored for Carolina (7-2-1). Devin Cooley made 34 stops for his first win of the season. His season's record improved to 1-2. Brandon Bussi, who had 31 stops for the defending Stanley Cup champions, took the loss to fall to 2-2-1. The game was scoreless into the second period when Kotkaniemi opened the scoring at 6:09, jamming in a rebound from the top of the crease. The goal came on Carolina's 19th shot of the game as Cooley had made a series of spectacular saves to keep the game scoreless. It was a tremendous bounceback effort for Cooley, who in his last start 10 days ago, was beaten seven times on 30 shots by the Colorado Avalanche. Dustin Wolf had started the last three games for the Flames. On the game-winner at 15:32 of the third, Frost sent a perfect saucer pass across the slot to Sharangovich, who one-timed it as soon as the puck landed on his stick and picked the top corner, sending Bussi's water bottle flying. Hurricanes: Mark Jankowski (lower body) was unable to play. items.title: Blues Recall Otto Stenberg, Place Ross Johnston On IR
items.summary: The St. Louis Blues have recalled forward Otto Stenberg and placed winger Ross Johnston (lower body) on injured reserve.
items.body: Register Login Blues Recall Otto Stenberg, Place Ross Johnston On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 9:30 pm The Blues have made a pair of roster moves late in the day. The team announced that they have recalled forward Otto Stenberg from AHL Springfield. To make room on the roster, winger Ross Johnston was placed on injured reserve. Stenberg was a first-round pick by St. Louis back in 2023, going 25th overall out of the junior ranks in Sweden. The 21-year-old made the jump to the SHL level in 2024-25 for his first extended taste of professional action before moving to North America midway through that season. He split the 2025-26 campaign between the Blues and Thunderbirds. In 32 games with the former, Stenberg held his own with 10 points in 32 games while averaging 13:37 per night of ice time. Meanwhile, in Springfield, he was a bit more productive, notching 17 points, though just four goals, in 37 appearances. This season, Stenberg has played exclusively in the minors, picking up a goal and three helpers in six games in the early going. As for Johnston, he missed last night’s game due to a lower-body injury. The 32-year-old is in the first season of a three-year, $6MM contract signed in free agency this summer and has one assist and 27 hits through his first six games. He’s officially listed as day-to-day, though he’ll have to miss a week of action due to this placement, which can be backdated to Friday. This recall keeps the Blues at a full 23-player roster but it also pushes their spending past the $104MM cap ceiling and into LTIR, meaning that they will stop accruing bankable cap space for the time being.

items.title: Salary Cap Deep Dive: Seattle Kraken
items.summary: A closer look at the salary cap situation for the Seattle Kraken for the 2026-27 season and beyond.
items.body: Register Login Salary Cap Deep Dive: Seattle Kraken By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 9:00 pm Navigating the salary cap is one of the most important tasks for a front office. Teams that can avoid total cap chaos by walking the tightrope of inking players to deals that match their value (or compensate for future value without breaking the bank) remain successful. Those who don’t often see struggles and front office changes. As we do each year, PHR will look at every NHL team and give a thorough look at their cap situation for the 2026-27 season, though in a slightly different format than before. This will focus more on players who are regulars on the roster versus those who may find themselves shuttling between the AHL and NHL. All cap figures are courtesy of PuckPedia . We’re currently covering the Pacific Division, next up are the Kraken. Upper Limit: $104MM Current Cap Charge: $87,834,576 Cap Space: $16,165,424 Potential Bonuses: $4.0625MM (less than $1MM likely to be reached) Dead Cap: $379,147 ( Joe Veleno buyout) Expiring Contracts (RFA): D Ryker Evans ($2.05MM), D Ville Ottavainen ($850K), F Shane Wright ($886,666 + $1MM in ‘A’ bonuses, $2.0625MM in ‘B’ bonuses) Wright’s reported desire for a change of scenery failed to materialize this summer so he’ll try to turn things around in Seattle. At this point, neither side likely wants to do a long-term deal so a bridge agreement is likely. Given where the market has moved, a similar showing to his first two years would yield an AAV around the $4.5MM mark. His B bonuses are extremely unlikely to be hit while he might hit one or two of his four A ones. Evans took a bit of a step back in the first year of his bridge contract last season. Still, he has second-pairing upside along with some potential offensive upside.

items.title: Penguins Recall Ilya Solovyov
items.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins have recalled defenseman Ilya Solovyov from AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton.
items.body: Register Login Penguins Recall Ilya Solovyov By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 7:31 pm It didn’t take long for the Penguins to fill the roster spot created when they sent Ryan Johnson down to the AHL earlier today. However, it’s not being filled by an IR activation. Instead, the team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve recalled blueliner Ilya Solovyov from AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. The 25-year-old bounced around a bit last season. He started training camp in Calgary but was plucked off waivers by Colorado in training camp. Then, a few months later, he was moved to Pittsburgh. Overall, Solovyov played in 30 NHL games between the two teams in 2025-26, notching one goal and seven assists while averaging 12:45 per game of ice time. While that was enough to earn him a one-year deal back in May, it wasn’t enough to secure Solovyov an NHL roster spot as he passed through waivers unclaimed this time a week and a half ago. He has one assist in three games with Wilkes-Barre/Scranton thus far. Solovyov will need to play in 32 NHL games this season for him to be a restricted free agent next summer. If he doesn’t do so, he’ll become a Group Six unrestricted free agent instead. With the recall, Pittsburgh’s 23-player roster is now full. At the moment, injured blueliners Trevor van Riemsdyk and Ryan Graves aren’t expected to join the team for Monday’s game in Utah but both are believed to be close to returning. They will need open roster spots to be activated off IR which means Solovyov’s stint with the big club could be a short one.

items.title: Maple Leafs Recall Vinni Lettieri, Place John Tavares On IR
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have recalled forward Vinni Lettieri from AHL Toronto while placing center John Tavares on injured reserve.
items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Recall Vinni Lettieri, Place John Tavares On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 6:59 pm When it was announced yesterday that Maple Leafs center John Tavares was out week-to-week, a recall from the minors was expected. That recall is center Vinni Lettieri , who has been recalled from AHL Toronto, per the NHL’s Media Site. The 31-year-old is in his second season with the Maple Leafs but has yet to make his first appearance with them. Instead, he has played exclusively with the Marlies as one of their top offensive players while making a one-way salary. He’s off to a strong start to his 2026-27 season, tallying three goals and six assists through his first five appearances to earn this promotion. Lettieri has seen NHL action in parts of seven seasons with four different teams so far in his career. His best season came in 2023-24 with Minnesota when he got into 46 games, collecting five goals and four assists. Over those seven years, he has 15 goals and 17 helpers in 155 appearances. Lettieri’s recall gives Toronto 13 healthy forwards on its active roster with still one roster spot available after Tavares was moved to injured reserve today. That will likely change over the next couple of days with Dakota Joshua ’s LTIR conditioning loan set to end early next week. Adding him back to the active roster could be enough insurance for Lettieri’s recall to only be a short-term one although they have the cap and roster space to have both around.

items.title: Flyers place Cam York on injured reserve
items.summary: York is averaging 21:49 of ice time through five games with the Flyers in 2026-27.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Daniel Kucin Jr.-Imagn Images The Philadelphia Flyers announced on social media that defenseman Cam York has been placed on injured reserve retroactive to Oct. 8 with an upper-body injury. The Flyers recalled defenseman Hunter McDonald from their AHL affiliate, the Lehigh Valley Phantoms. Forward Jack Studnicka and defender Helge Grans were also loaned to the Phantoms. York, 25, suffered the injury during the team’s team’s 2-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators on Oct. 8. Through five games in 2026-27, the left-handed blueliner is averaging 21:49 of ice time. Now in his seventh season, York, taken No. 14 overall in the 2019 NHL Entry Draft, has 23 goals and 80 assists for 103 points in 314 career regular-season contests. He’s in the second season of a five-year contract that carries a cap hit of $5.15 million. As for McDonald, the 24-year-old defender has spent the last two seasons with the Phantoms. Through parts of four AHL seasons, he has five goals and 25 assists for 30 points and 205 penalty minutes in 153 career regular-season games. A sixth-round pick for the Flyers in 2022, the Fairport, N.Y., native played two seasons of college hockey at Northeastern University. In 58 career NCAA games, McDonald had two goals and 18 assists for 20 points and 88 penalty minutes. The Flyers are 1-6-3 with five points through 10 games in 2026-27. They won their first of the season Saturday night with a 3-1 victory over the Senators, thanks to a pair of two-point performances from Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone. Trevor Zegras also potted his second of the season.

items.body: Register Login Penguins Reassign Ryan Johnson By Brennan McClain | at October 18, 2026 5:00 pm According to a team announcement , the Pittsburgh Penguins have reassigned defenseman Ryan Johnson to the AHL’s Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. The roster move opens the door for Pittsburgh to return Samuel Girard and Trevor van Riemsdyk to the lineup tomorrow against the Utah Mammoth. The Penguins recently acquired Johnson from the Buffalo Sabres on October 12th. That’s the same day Pittsburgh placed van Riemsdyk on the injured reserve with a lower-body injury. Girard was injured in Pittsburgh’s recent contest against the Vegas Golden Knights, though it was never considered overly serious. Despite being on the Penguins’ roster since they acquired him, Johnson served only as an extra defenseman if needed. The former first-round pick will continue the 2026-27 season having only played in the AHL. He went scoreless in four games with the AHL’s Rochester Americans to begin the campaign. Once considered a quality defensive prospect for the Sabres, Johnson’s career hasn’t played out as hoped. Since turning pro in the 2023-24 campaign, Johnson has scored seven goals and 41 points in 153 AHL contests with a +8 rating. In the NHL, Johnson has registered seven assists in 47 games, averaging 13:48 of ice time per game. Regardless of Johnson’s demotion, the Penguins will essentially return to a fully healthy defensive corps tomorrow evening. Veteran Ryan Graves is expected to return from his lower-body injury within the next week, though Pittsburgh isn’t expected to keep him on the roster long. Even at a $4.5MM salary, Graves’ contract is bloated for what he offers, and he’ll easily pass through waivers, as he did last season.

Minnesota announced they’ve recalled forward Hunter Haight and defenseman Carson Lambos from the AHL’s Iowa Wild. items.body: Register Login Blackhawks Reassign Dominic Toninato By Brennan McClain | at October 18, 2026 3:00 pm According to a team announcement , the Chicago Blackhawks have assigned forward Dominic Toninato to the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs. Toninato is expected to play for the IceHogs tonight against the Grand Rapids Griffins. It’s a procedural move by the Blackhawks. With a five-day break until their next contest, Chicago has chosen to delay Toninato’s waiver eligibility. Once a player clears waivers, they don’t become eligible again until they’ve cumulatively played in 10 games or spent 30 days on the roster. Currently, Toninato has played in three games and spent 11 days on the Blackhawks. However, if they want him back by next Friday, Toninato must play for Rockford this afternoon. To protect against paper transactions, a player must play in one AHL contest after reassignment to be eligible for another recall. The Blackhawks don’t play again until October 23rd. After today, Rockford’s next game isn’t until the 24th. Still, unless there’s another injury, Toninato’s next recall should be his last for some time. Although he’ll likely be unavailable against the Montreal Canadiens, forward Andrew Mangiapan e is expected to be activated from the injured reserve shortly thereafter. Toninato, 32, is in his second season with Chicago after spending half a decade with the Winnipeg Jets. In his three games as an injury replacement, Toninato went scoreless while averaging 8:52 of ice time. Today’s contest will be his second with Rockford this season. items.title: Maple Leafs fall into last in Atlantic with loss to Islanders
items.summary: What the Maple Leafs can do now is summon urgency as they enter Week 4 of 2026-27 in the same spot they finished 2025-26: last place in the Atlantic Division.
items.body: When do the good vibes bubbling around the Toronto Maple Leafs ’ early season need to translate to meaningful growth? Hat tricks and highlights and rookie intrigue and some impressive individual showings will only get a team so far. Now, we see how the house that John Chayka built holds up to its first real stretch of severe weather: injuries to two backbone players, three consecutive losses, and a tumble down the standings despite playing twice as many games at home as on the road. Sometime after Troy Stecher — an admirable third-pair defenceman playing top-pair minutes Saturday — takes his stick and smashes it in half over Sergei Bobrovsky’s crossbar in frustration, and sometime before a few Leafs faithful let the boo birds fly and head coach Jim Hiller delivers his tensest post-game press conference since the last one, it dawns on you: Maybe the Maple Leafs (3-4-2) aren’t significantly better than they were under the last coach. The New York Islanders, who beat the home team 4-1 wire-to-wire Saturday, aren’t considered an NHL powerhouse by any means. The Leafs are down Chris Tanev and John Tavares, sure. But they’re rested and should’ve been inspired to respond from Thursday’s blown two-goal lead to Buffalo. And the patient, pack-the-house Islanders started the game down Mathew Barzal and lost two more top-six forwards to injury before the game was 17 minutes old. Still, Toronto could not find a path — or opted not to force one — through Pete DeBoer’s defence. “It’s just disappointing. They could have their full lineup in there, and our lack of fortitude to get to the inside makes it disappointing in any case,” Hiller lamented. “You’re not going to score from the perimeter against this team. “I don’t think our D had many looks tonight, and there was nothing inside.”

items.title: Panthers become first NHL team to record natural hat trick in three straight games
items.summary: The Panthers also became the first team in more than 100 years to have at least four hat tricks in the first 10 games of a season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida Panthers forward Carter Verhaeghe recorded a natural hat trick during the team’s 8-3 win over the Seattle Kraken Saturday night. Verhaeghe’s trio of goals made the Panthers the first team in NHL history with natural hat tricks in three consecutive games, after Brady Tkachuk recorded a natural hat trick in Florida’s previous two games. Verhaeghe scored twice late in the first period, then again midway through the second. Panthers forward Sam Bennett also recorded a hat trick in Saturday’s game. Now with four on the season, Florida became the first team in more than 100 years to record four or more hat tricks before its 10th game of the season (the Toronto St. Patricks, later named the Toronto Maple Leafs, had five in 1922-23). The Panthers recorded its first of three natural hat tricks when forward Brady Tkachuk scored three straight in the second period of the team’s 7-3 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets last Tuesday. His brother, Matthew Tkachuk, assisted on all three goals. On Thursday, Brady Tkachuk became the first NHLer to record back-to-back natural hat tricks in Florida’s 3-2 overtime win against the Vancouver Canucks . The Panthers are now 5-2-2 through nine games in 2026-27. Matthew Tkatchuk leads the team with 11 assists and 14 points, while Brady Tkachuk and Verhaeghe are tied for a team-leading six goals. Defenseman Seth Jones has one goal and nine assists for 10 points.

items.title: Cole Caufield scores overtime winner as Canadiens down Sabres
items.body: Cole Caufield scored twice, including the overtime winner, to lift the Montreal Canadiens past the Buffalo Sabres 4-3 on Saturday night. Caufield went on a breakaway after Josh Norris missed his shot on a three-on-one rush before ripping a shot into the top-left corner 54 seconds into the extra period. Zachary Bolduc and Alexandre Texier also scored as Montreal (4-3-1) built a two-goal lead before Buffalo stormed back. Juraj Slafkovsky and Alexandre Carrier added two assists each. Jacob Fowler stopped 23 shots in his fourth start in five games. Jack Quinn, Tage Thompson and Norris replied for Buffalo (4-3-2), which fell 4-3 in a shootout to the Canadiens on Tuesday. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 30 saves. Thompson tied the game 3-3 with 9:48 remaining in the third period after Josh Doan found him alone at the side of the net to eventually force overtime. Norris opened the scoring for the Sabres at 8:21 in a sluggish first period for the Canadiens, tallying his second goal this season on a rebound after Montreal defenceman David Reinbacher turned the puck over in the neutral zone. The Canadiens broke out of a sluggish start with a tying goal on their first shot. Bolduc was promoted to Montreal’s top power-play unit and tipped in Nick Suzuki’s wrist shot at 11:45 of the opening period for his fourth of the campaign. Caufield made it 2-1 for Montreal at 14:01 when he hammered a shot past an unsuspecting Luukkonen after Slafkovsky beat Olen Zellweger to a loose puck behind Buffalo’s net. Texier buried a rebound at 7:39 in the second period. Quinn responded two minutes later with a short-handed goal assisted by Zach Benson after a heads-up dump-in from Mattias Samuelsson, cutting Montreal’s lead to 3-2 after 40 minutes. items.title: Jets discuss Hellebuyck’s potential return
items.body: Scott Arniel took the podium Saturday afternoon to break down a hockey match, only to provide his two cents on a growing and unpredictable game of chicken involving his NHL club. The Winnipeg Jets head coach spoke less than three minutes following a 3-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes at Canada Life Centre — a game entirely overshadowed by the latest chapter in franchise goaltender Connor Hellebuyck's ongoing trade holdout. “I really don’t care right now on that scenario," started a visibly frustrated Arniel. "My focus is we’ve got St. Louis coming up. I’ve got to do some review against Carolina, there are some areas I want to fix." Just minutes before puck drop, it was reported that Hellebuyck notified the Jets on Oct. 2 — before Winnipeg's first regular-season game — that he planned to end his absence. Rather than welcoming the star netminder back into the fold immediately, the Jets opted to leverage the NHL's collective bargaining agreement. According to reports, the club used Article 15.13, subsection (c)(v) to suspend Hellebuyck for three weeks for failure to report to training camp. The suspension is set to expire on Friday, Oct. 23, just two days before Winnipeg hosts the Montreal Canadiens in the annual Heritage Classic outdoor game at Princess Auto Stadium. "That part, that falls down on Chevy," noted Arniel, noting whatever happens next will be handled by general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff. "I know there is stuff that happens. I’m going to face that one when it happens." "I don’t know what next week is going to look like and at the end of the day, for me, I’ve got 23 guys and all they care about is winning hockey games," added Arniel. items.title: Flyers top Senators to secure first win of season, snap nine-game skid
items.body: With a 3-1 decision on Saturday night against the Ottawa Senators , the Flyers earned their first victory of the season. The win also served to snap the nine-game winless skid to start the season, which was a franchise record. It looked to be the same story for the Flyers as Senators forward Drake Batherson opened the scoring in the second period. But Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone made quick work to negate the deficit, combining for two goals to close out the middle frame. Trevor Zegras added an insurance empty-netter in the third period as the Flyers wrapped up the win. It's a welcome bit of good news for the Flyers, who dug themselves a deep hole early after ending last season with a run to the Eastern Conference semifinals. The Flyers sit in the basement of the East standings and while the season is still young, they'll have to string together more wins like Saturday to claw their way back to relevance.

It wasn't immediately clear what forced the 29-year-old blue-liner to exit, but Chabot was seen shaking his hand in the penalty box in the first period. items.title: Maple Leafs would deal prime asset for difference-maker on blue line
items.body: With Chris Tanev sidelined for multiple weeks with an upper-body injury, the Toronto Maple Leafs could look to make a splash in order to boost their defensive corps. Although Tanev skated on Saturday, the Maple Leafs have made it clear that they aren't interested in a "Band-Aid solution" to fill the open spot, according to Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman. "(The Maple Leafs) have said that they will pay a premium asset if they believe that they are getting a difference-maker on the blue line," Friedman reported on the latest segment of Saturday Headlines . "They've told people they're not moving what they consider 'A-assets' for a B-level replacement." Toronto head coach Jim Hillier said Thursday that he is comfortable with the defenceman currently on the Maple Leafs' roster, but added that it would take a team effort to replace Tanev's impact. The 36-year-old defenceman was hurt in Toronto's 6-3 road win over the Colorado Avalanche last Saturday and placed on injured reserve Monday. Tanev skated in five shifts in the first period before leaving the game. The oft-injured Tanev was limited to 11 games last season due to spine and groin injuries as well as a concussion. He has one assist in six games this season. In its first two games without Tanev, Toronto surrendered 10 total goals across a pair of 5-4 losses to the Utah Mammoth and Buffalo Sabres. Adding a defenceman who can step in and contribute right away isn't the only type of move being considered for the Maple Leafs' roster. "They've also indicated that they would consider getting a younger player (by) moving an older guy," Friedman said Saturday. "So, that's what Toronto is looking at right now." The Maple Leafs currently have the fourth oldest roster in the NHL by average age.

items.title: Canucks’ disheartening, winless road trip still features silver linings
items.summary: This six-game road trip was awfully disheartening for the Canucks, but certainly not a waste of time for a team trying to find its way.
items.body: It wasn’t so much a road trip as a six-game educational tour that the Vancouver Canucks finished Saturday in Tampa. They discovered how much they don’t know. More constructively, they discovered how much room they have for learning in the coming months (and years) as the National Hockey League team’s rebuild gets going. Over six games in 12 days, which included three opponents who have combined for five of the last seven Stanley Cup championships, the Canucks were schooled. Sometimes, brutally so. Their 4-2 loss Saturday to the Tampa Bay Lightning capped a winless road trip in which the Canucks claimed just one of 12 points available — and even that one, from Thursday’s overtime loss to the Florida Panthers, was a consolation prize for blowing a two-goal lead in the final nine minutes of regulation time. Vancouver had another 2-0 lead in Tampa, thanks primarily to spectacular goaltending from Kevin Lankinen, but surrendered four unanswered goals over the final 34 minutes. “It’s obviously disappointing to come away from a trip with one point,” Canucks coach Manny Malhotra told reporters in Tampa. “And just the way we're giving up points and goals, it continues to frustrate the group. But you know. . . a lot of the things that we see are fixable.
